text:
The Lightning reassigned Dominic James to the AHL's Syracuse Crunch on Nov. 4, along with Cooper Flinton. He played six games, with 2 assists, before the move. That's the headline, and the numbers explain it.

In those six games, Tampa took 31% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with James on the ice at five on five, 28 points worse than without him. That's a tiny sample, and his on-ice shot attempts were close to even (50%), so the chances against were the issue rather than the volume. He didn't score on 0.67 expected goals.

There's a real player here. He's a 2022 sixth-round pick who scored 30 points in 35 games at Minnesota Duluth before turning pro, and he played 43 NHL games last season with 15 points. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found a signature: 18% of his setups go across the royal road, the side-to-side pass that moves a goalie, and over half his shots come off the rush. On a Lightning team rolling at home, there was no room to learn on the job. We'd expect him back when injuries hit.
headline: Dominic James heads to Syracuse
